candidates.label: numberOfPreviousOwners
candidates.comment: The total number of previous owners of a vehicle, including the current owner. Also called prior owners, owner history count, past owners. Examples: "Used Car A numberOfPreviousOwners 1", "Vintage Vehicle B numberOfPreviousOwners 3", "New Car C numberOfPreviousOwners 0".

candidates.label: episodeNumber
candidates.comment: An episode number relation between an episode and the integer or text representing its position within an ordered group. Also called "episode index", "sequence number", "part number". Examples: "Episode 'The Pilot' episodeNumber '1'", "TV episode episodeNumber 'Season 3, Episode 7'", "Podcast episode episodeNumber '42'".

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: successorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a newer product model and its previous, often discontinued, predecessor. Also called "replaces", "evolved from", "preceded by", "derived from". Examples: "iPhone 15 is successorOf iPhone 14", "The new car model is successorOf the previous generation", "This product is a successorOf an older variant."

candidates.label: orderNumber
candidates.comment: An identifier for an entire order or transaction. Also called transaction ID, purchase order number, order ID. Examples: "Customer Order orderNumber 'PO-12345'", "Online Transaction orderNumber 'TXN-67890'", "Sales Order orderNumber 'SO-001'". Distinct from orderItemNumber, which identifies a specific item within an order.

candidates.label: serialNumber
candidates.comment: A unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to a specific individual product. Also called product ID, unique identifier, item serial. Examples: `Laptop` serialNumber `"C02X12345678"`, `Offer for Phone` serialNumber `"SN12345ABC"`, `Demand for Specific Part` serialNumber `"XYZ98765"`. Distinct from `sku`, which is a merchant-specific identifier for a *type* of product, not an individual one.

candidates.label: currentExchangeRate

candidates.label: confirmationNumber
candidates.comment: An identification relation for an invoice or order, providing a number that confirms its receipt. Also called "order confirmation", "booking reference", "receipt number". Examples: "Online order confirmationNumber 'ABC-12345'", "Flight invoice confirmationNumber 'XYZ-67890'".

candidates.label: serialNumber

Distinct from `sku`, which is a merchant-specific identifier for a *type* of product, not an individual one.

candidates.label: orderItemNumber
candidates.comment: An identifier for a specific order item. Also called item ID, line item number, order line identifier. Examples: "OrderItem A orderItemNumber '001'", "OrderItem B orderItemNumber 'SKU-456'", "OrderItem C orderItemNumber 'LITM-789'". Distinct from orderNumber, which identifies the entire order.

candidates.label: reportNumber
candidates.comment: A report number relation between a report and the unique identifier assigned by its publisher. Also called report ID, document number. Examples: "A financial report has a report number 'FY2023-Q4'.", "A technical report has a report number 'TR-001-2024'.", "A government report has a report number 'GAO-24-123'."

candidates.label: catalogNumber
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a music release and its unique catalog number. Also called "release ID", "record label number", "product number". Examples: "Album release catalogNumber 'ABC-123'", "Single release catalogNumber 'XYZ-456'".

candidates.label: clipNumber
candidates.comment: A positional relation for a clip, indicating its order within a group of clips. Also called "clip index", "clip position", "sequence number". Examples: "Video clip clipNumber 3", "Audio clip clipNumber 'Part 1'".

candidates.label: trackingNumber
candidates.comment: A tracking number relation between a parcel delivery and its unique identifier provided by the shipper. Also called shipment ID, parcel ID, delivery tracking code. Examples: "ParcelDelivery trackingNumber '1Z999AA10123456784'", "ParcelDelivery trackingNumber 'JD0001234567890123'", "ParcelDelivery trackingNumber '9400100000000000000000'".

candidates.label: busNumber
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a bus trip and its unique identifier. Also called "bus ID", "bus route number", "bus identifier". Examples: "Bus trip from NYC to Boston busNumber 'B101'", "Local route 10 bus trip busNumber '4567'". Distinct from busName, which is a human-readable name, whereas busNumber is a unique identifier.

relations.definition: Indicates the reason or factor leading to a particular outcome.
relations.embedding_query_text: cause: Indicates the reason or factor leading to a particular outcome.

instances: Conflict making outbreak difficult to tackle -> Bundibugyo virus

chosen_property.label: cause
chosen_property.justification: The 'cause' property directly represents the causal relationship, where the object is the cause of the subject, fitting the relation phrase.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: diagnosis
candidates.comment: A diagnostic outcome relation between a DDx element or patient and one or more alternative medical conditions considered in the differential diagnosis process. Also called: medical diagnosis, differential diagnosis, identified condition. Examples: "Patient X" diagnosis "Common Cold", "DDx Element" diagnosis "Influenza", "Medical Case" diagnosis "Allergic Reaction". Distinct from differentialDiagnosis, which is the set of competing diagnoses.

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: riskFactor
candidates.comment: A factor that increases the likelihood of a patient developing a specific medical condition. Also called predisposing factor, risk element, vulnerability factor. Examples: `Heart Disease` riskFactor `High Cholesterol`, `Diabetes` riskFactor `Obesity`, `Lung Cancer` riskFactor `Smoking`.

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

relations.definition: Indicates an entity's authority or power over a region or resource.

chosen_property.label: owns
chosen_property.justification: The 'owns' property is the closest fit for indicating an entity's authority or power over a region, implying a form of ownership or control.

candidates.label: accessibilityControl
candidates.comment: An accessibility control relation between a creative work and the input methods sufficient for its full control. Also called control methods, input compatibility, interaction modes. Examples: "A video game's accessibility control is 'keyboard'.", "A web application's accessibility control is 'mouse'."

candidates.label: affectedRegion
candidates.comment: Indicates the geographical region that was impacted by an event.

candidates.label: regionsAllowed
candidates.comment: A regions allowed relation between a media object and the geographical areas where its use is permitted. Also called allowed in, permitted regions, geographical availability. Examples: "A movie streaming service has regions allowed 'US, Canada'.", "A music video has regions allowed 'Europe'.", "A software download has regions allowed 'Worldwide'."

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: jurisdiction
candidates.comment: A legal scope relation between a government service or legislation and the administrative area or territory where it applies. Also called legal authority, governing area, applicable region, domain of law. Examples: A government service has a jurisdiction of 'California'. Legislation has a jurisdiction of 'United States federal law'. A permit applies to the jurisdiction of 'City of London'. Distinct from eligibleRegion or ineligibleRegion, which are about availability, not legal authority.

candidates.label: license
candidates.comment: A licensing relation between a creative work and the license document that applies to its content. Also called: governed by license, licensed under, copyright license. Examples: "Software Project license MIT License", "Image license Creative Commons Attribution 4.0", "Music Track license Public Domain".

candidates.label: hasSource

candidates.comment: Indicates the origin or source of a claim, observation, or information.

candidates.label: constraintProperty
candidates.comment: A definitional relation for a constraint node, indicating a property used as a constraint. Also called "constraining property", "restricted by property", "property constraint". Examples: "Statistical variable constraint node constraintProperty 'schema:age'", "Data filter constraintProperty 'dc:gender'".

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

candidates.label: permissions
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the permissions required for a software application to function. Also called access requirements, app permissions, authorization needs. Examples: A mobile app requires permissions for 'full internet access'. A software application requires permissions for 'access to camera'. A game requires permissions for 'storage access'.

candidates.label: numberOfBeds

Examples: "King Bed Details numberOfBeds 1", "Twin Bed Details numberOfBeds 2", "Queen Bed Details numberOfBeds 1". Distinct from numberOfBedrooms, which specifies the number of rooms designated as bedrooms.

candidates.label: wordCount
candidates.comment: A word count relation between a creative work and an integer, indicating the total number of words in its text. Also called text length, word total, lexical count. Examples: Article wordCount 1500, Book wordCount 80000, BlogPosting wordCount 750.

candidates.label: numberOfDoors
candidates.comment: The number of doors on a vehicle. Also called door count, vehicle doors, doors quantity. Examples: "Sedan X numberOfDoors 4", "Coupe Y numberOfDoors 2", "Hatchback Z numberOfDoors 5".

candidates.label: commentCount
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement for a creative work, indicating the total number of comments it has received. Also called "number of comments", "comment total", "feedback count". Examples: "Blog post commentCount 15", "Article commentCount 200".

candidates.label: taxonomicRange
